narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Picture Board"**

The unit is read from three metres as icons, figures and numbers, with almost no sentences. A charge nurse at 07:00 sees which rooms to worry about and what the unit will be short of in the next 24 hours without reading a paragraph. The ground is a cool grey, the cards are white with soft corners, and there is one blue. Everything on the board is either ink or blue: ink means now, blue means forecast.

Colour outside that pair is rationed to meaning. Amber appears for TIGHT and BUSY, red for SHORT and VERY BUSY and the highest-risk person figure, and green for Leaving borders and labels and for ON TRACK and USUAL. Leaving figures fill in secondary ink (grey). Every status is carried three ways at once, by a fill or border, a drawn shape and a word. There are two boards, day and night, and both are first-class: they swap custom properties and nothing else.
keyCharacteristics: Ink is now, blue is the next 24 hours.
Pictures before words: one drawn icon family, solid for running, outline for expected.
Every bed is drawn as a change: Now, an arrow, Next 24 h.
Chances are whole percentages ("23%"), "<5%" when very small, "No estimate" when null.
Two boards (day, night) with the same grammar; wall screens scale the root to 120% from 1800px.
Two tabs only: Bed board (default) and Unit strain.

rules.name: The Ink and Blue Rule
rules.body: Ink means now, blue means forecast. A count, icon or figure in ink is happening at 07:00; the same thing in blue is expected in the next 24 hours. Never use blue for decoration or for a link.

rules.name: The Rationed Colour Rule
rules.body: Amber for TIGHT and BUSY. Red for SHORT and VERY BUSY and the highest-risk person figure. Green for Leaving borders and labels and for ON TRACK and USUAL. Red never fills a bed tile; leaving figures fill in secondary ink (grey).

rules.name: The Three Carriers Rule
rules.body: Status is never colour alone. Each status has a fill or border, a shape and a word.

rules.name: The Count Rule
rules.body: A chance is a whole percentage on every screen ("23%"), "<5%" when very small, and "No estimate" when it is null (2026-11-14 evening; this replaces the earlier natural frequencies). The room page keeps its 10-dot array as the picture beside the percentage. The lines that flag a bed are chosen by the team (default 25%, Worsening at the next step up, Leaving 60%).

rules.name: The Range Rule
rules.body: Every forecast count carries its range in Caption weight 400 beside it ("+3" then "1 to 5").

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: There is a card shadow and a floating shadow. Nothing else lifts. Hover moves a tile or figure up 1px over .15s; it does not add shadow.

dos: Do draw now in ink and forecast in blue, on every surface.
Do write chances as whole percentages ("23%"), "<5%" when very small, and "No estimate" for null.
Do carry every status as a fill or border, a shape and a word.
Do show the range beside every forecast count.
Do use solid icons for support running now and outline icons for support expected.
Do keep every target at least 2.75rem (44px) tall and all text at 4.5:1 or better on both boards.
Do change only custom properties between the day and night boards.
Do keep to the five predictions: IMV, vasopressor, CRRT, leaving the ICU, death.
donts: Don't let death colour or mark a bed. It is a plain count on Unit strain and a plain row on the room page.
Don't use red outside SHORT, VERY BUSY and the highest-risk person figure; never fill a bed tile red.
Don't signal status by colour alone.
Don't use signal-bar glyphs or letter tags (V, P, C) for supports.
Don't add pulsing or looping animation.
Don't write hedging or disclaimer copy on the board.
Don't add a sixth prediction or a forecast count without its range.
Don't bring in icons from an external set; extend the drawn family on the 24 grid.
